main_concerns.concern: The review package treats a self-check run with --skip-carrier-probe as validating evidence, while the carrier probe is exactly the component needed to test the remaining risk (project-level hooks and role session IDs). This produces a satisfying validation narrative while bypassing the hardest verification step.

--ignore-user-config is a broad suppression flag that may suppress more user-level config than the targeted interactive brainstorming skill. Without a carrier probe or actual E2E run, there is no evidence the flag does not also interfere with project-level or role-level configurations needed for correct E2E operation. The self-check passed with --skip-carrier-probe, which directly contradicts the acceptance contract's new requirement for independent carrier-probe verification of project-level hooks and session behavior.

minimum_fixes.minimum_fix: Do not commit or declare readiness until the carrier probe is included: rerun the full RedCap check and a fresh E2E round, then attach the actual diff and Round 20 hook-events-summary / role session-ID evidence. Only then treat the patch as validated.

Before running Round 20: (1) execute a carrier probe with --ignore-user-config enabled to verify project-level hooks still fire, (2) log which specific user-level configs are being suppressed vs preserved, and (3) do not skip the carrier probe in the Round 20 self-check. If the carrier probe reveals any suppressed config that E2E roles depend on, narrow the suppression to target only interactive/approval-gating skills rather than all user config.
